claims.text: As-built AlCrFeNiSi miniature components produced by high-thermal-load additive manufacturing exhibit significant residual thermal stresses.
Rapid thermal cycling in high-thermal-load additive manufacturing degrades the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Rapid thermal cycling produces complex microstructural features in as-built AlCrFeNiSi components.
A single low-temperature annealing post-processing step can relieve residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi components.
Low-temperature annealing can improve the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi components.
Annealing AlCrFeNiSi at 300–400°C for around one hour is sufficient to permit atomic rearrangement.
Annealing AlCrFeNiSi at 300–400°C for around one hour avoids full recrystallization.
Low-temperature annealing develops multiscale chemical short-range order in AlCrFeNiSi.
Chemical short-range order relieves thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
Chemical short-range order enhances the yield strength of AlCrFeNiSi.
Low-temperature annealing enables controlled atomic diffusion that relieves built-in thermal stresses.
Annealing-induced atomic ordering produces a more resilient microstructure that resists softening.
Annealing-induced short-range order maintains a favorable balance between strength and ductility.
Relative to untreated high-thermal-load AM components, annealed AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual stress.
Relative to untreated high-thermal-load AM components, annealed AlCrFeNiSi components will have higher yield strength.
Relative to untreated high-thermal-load AM components, annealed AlCrFeNiSi components will maintain or improve ductility.
Restricting annealing to 300–400°C avoids unwanted phase transformations in AlCrFeNiSi.
Restricting annealing to 300–400°C avoids excessive grain growth in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed mechanism is transferred from evidence concerning a different complex alloy, identified as CoNiV rather than AlCrFeNiSi.
